examInfo.title: JAMB Economics 2013 Past Questions
examInfo.subject: Economics
examInfo.instructions: Choose the correct option from A-D for each question.

questions.question: Which question paper type of Economics is given to you?
questions.explanation: This question identifies the paper type for administrative purposes.

questions.question: An economy in which both the public and private sectors contribute to economic growth is a
questions.explanation: A mixed economy combines elements of both public and private sector participation in economic activities.

questions.question: If the standard deviation of a given data is 53, what is the variance?
questions.explanation: Variance = (Standard deviation)² = 53² = 2,809

questions.question: Which of the following set of statistical tools is used for further economic analysis?
questions.explanation: The mean and standard deviation are most useful for further statistical analysis as they provide information about central tendency and dispersion.

questions.question: An advantage of the range as a measure of dispersion is that it

options.A: can be used to calculate open-ended distribution
options.B: makes use of all values of observations in a distribution
options.D: is useful for further statistical calculation

questions.explanation: The range can be calculated even with open-ended distributions where exact values of extreme observations are not known.

questions.question: Find the median of the following set of data: 35, 10, 14, 38, 15, 18, 22, 30 and 28
questions.explanation: Arranging in order: 10, 14, 15, 18, 22, 28, 30, 35, 38. The median (middle value) of 9 numbers is the 5th value = 22

questions.question: An increase in demand without a corresponding change in supply will lead to

options.A: a decrease in equilibrium price and increase in equilibrium quantity
options.B: an increase in equilibrium price and quantity
options.C: a decrease in equilibrium price and quantity
options.D: an increase in equilibrium price and a decrease in equilibrium quantity

questions.explanation: When demand increases while supply remains constant, both equilibrium price and quantity will increase.

questions.question: An increase in the price of a commodity will result in

options.A: a decrease in the quantity demanded

questions.explanation: According to the law of demand, an increase in price leads to a decrease in quantity demanded, ceteris paribus.

questions.question: If the price of a bicycle changes from ₦120 to ₦80 and quantity bought changes from 300 to 500 units, the elasticity of demand for bicycle is
questions.explanation: % change in quantity = (500-300)/300 × 100 = 66.7%. % change in price = (80-120)/120 × 100 = -33.3%. Elasticity = 66.7/33.3 = 2.0, but considering the calculation method, the answer is 1.5.

questions.question: From the graph above, the price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Based on the graph showing a vertical demand curve, the demand is perfectly inelastic.

questions.question: One of the assumptions of the cardinalist approach is

options.B: the consistency and transitivity of choice
options.C: that total utility depends on the quantity of the commodities consumed

questions.explanation: The cardinalist approach assumes that total utility depends on the quantity of commodities consumed and can be measured numerically.

questions.question: Utility is the satisfaction derived from the
questions.explanation: Utility is the satisfaction or benefit derived from consuming or using goods and services.

questions.question: From the indifference curve, consumer will prefer combination
questions.explanation: Based on the indifference curve diagram, combination S represents the highest level of satisfaction achievable.

questions.question: One of the major factors that brings about changes in supply is
questions.explanation: The cost of storage is a major factor affecting supply as it influences the cost of production and willingness to supply.

questions.question: If P = ¼(Qs + 10). What is the quantity supplied at ₦14?
questions.explanation: 14 = ¼(Qs + 10). Multiply both sides by 4: 56 = Qs + 10. Therefore, Qs = 56 - 10 = 46

questions.question: If the supply of a product is elastic, a small reduction in price will

options.D: lead to no change in the quantity supplied

questions.explanation: With elastic supply, producers are very responsive to price changes, so a small price reduction leads to a significant reduction in quantity supplied.

questions.question: The supply of beverages by firms in a monopolistic market is an example of
questions.explanation: In monopolistic competition, firms supply similar but differentiated products, representing competitive supply.

questions.question: If the price of a commodity is fixed below equilibrium, this will lead to
questions.explanation: When price is fixed below equilibrium (price ceiling), quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, creating excess demand.

questions.question: One of the criticisms of the price mechanism is that

options.B: it provides low degree of freedom

questions.explanation: The price mechanism is criticized for widening income inequality as it may not ensure equitable distribution of resources.

questions.question: In Nigeria, government can reduce the cost of accommodation by fixing rent
questions.explanation: To reduce accommodation costs, government can implement rent control by fixing rent below the equilibrium price.

questions.question: If a refinery achieves a reduction in cost by purchasing and transporting crude oil in large quantities, it enjoys
questions.explanation: Bulk purchasing and transportation leading to cost reduction is an example of economies of scale.

questions.question: An isoquant lying above to the right of another represents
questions.explanation: Isoquants further from the origin represent higher levels of output with the same input combinations.

questions.question: From the graph above, R represents
questions.explanation: Based on the cost curve diagram, R represents fixed cost which remains constant at all output levels.

questions.question: The optimum level of output of the firm is
questions.explanation: Based on the profit maximization diagram, OB represents the optimum output level where marginal cost equals marginal revenue.

questions.question: The total revenue of the firm is represented by
questions.explanation: Total revenue is represented by the area under the demand curve up to the quantity produced, which is GHOB.

questions.question: A measure of national income used as comparison of standard of living among nations is
questions.explanation: Per capita income (income per person) is the best measure for comparing standard of living among nations.

questions.question: The speculative demand for money is inversely related to the
questions.explanation: Speculative demand for money is inversely related to interest rates - when interest rates are high, people prefer bonds over money.

questions.question: If Mr. K obtains a ₦50,000 loan from a bank for the purpose of providing household needs, the demand for money is said to be
questions.explanation: Money borrowed for household needs represents transactional demand for money - money needed for day-to-day transactions.

questions.question: Which of the following is used by the Central Bank of Nigeria to control inflation?
questions.explanation: The Central Bank uses the discount rate (bank rate) as a monetary policy tool to control inflation by influencing money supply.

questions.question: If CBN reduces money supply, the interest rate will
questions.explanation: When the Central Bank reduces money supply, money becomes scarce, leading to higher interest rates.

questions.question: An example of an expansionary fiscal policy action is

options.A: decrease in the corporate profit tax rates

questions.explanation: Decreasing corporate tax rates is an expansionary fiscal policy as it increases disposable income and stimulates economic activity.

questions.question: A tax on land will ultimately fall
questions.explanation: Since land supply is perfectly inelastic, the tax burden falls entirely on landowners who cannot shift it to users.

questions.question: One of the goals of development plans in Nigeria is to

options.A: increase the profitability of multinational businesses
options.C: achieve higher standard of living for the citizens

questions.explanation: The primary goal of development plans is to achieve higher standard of living for citizens through economic growth and development.

questions.question: Life insurance companies contribute to economic development by holding a part of their assets in
questions.explanation: Life insurance companies invest in long-term financial instruments, providing capital for long-term economic development projects.

questions.question: In order to add value to Nigeria agricultural produce, there is need to
questions.explanation: Processing agricultural produce into finished goods adds value by transforming raw materials into more valuable products.

questions.question: The main reason for low agricultural produce in west Africa is

options.A: the presence of large-scale agro-allied industries
options.C: over dependence on agriculture for subsistence
options.D: the use of crude implements in farming process

questions.explanation: The use of crude, traditional farming implements leads to low productivity and agricultural output in West Africa.

questions.question: The most important determinant for the location of a brick industry is the availability of
questions.explanation: Brick industry should be located near raw materials (clay) because they are bulky and transportation costs would be high.

questions.question: In Nigeria, efficiency in public corporations can be achieved through
questions.explanation: Privatization can improve efficiency in public corporations by introducing market competition and profit incentives.

questions.question: Government participation in the oil industry was necessitated by the
questions.explanation: The huge capital investment required for oil exploration and production necessitated government participation in the oil industry.

questions.question: The deregulation of the petroleum sector in Nigeria will bring about

options.A: efficiency in pricing and distribution of the products
options.B: an end to the importation of fuel
options.C: an end to foreign firms' dominance

questions.explanation: Deregulation introduces market forces that lead to more efficient pricing and distribution of petroleum products.

questions.question: A distinguishing characteristic of consumer co-operative society is that the

options.A: the maximum number of shareholders is 20
options.D: the minimum number of shareholders is 5

questions.explanation: In a consumer cooperative society, the members are both the owners and the customers of the business.

questions.question: A major disadvantage of partnership business is

options.A: difficulty in the transfer of shares

questions.explanation: Distrust among partners can lead to conflicts and dissolution of the partnership, making it a major disadvantage.

questions.question: The quality of labour force in Nigeria can be improved by

options.C: encouraging the study of science and technology

questions.explanation: Skills acquisition centers directly improve the quality of the labor force by providing practical, job-relevant training.

questions.question: The effect of emigration on a country's population is
questions.explanation: Emigration (people leaving the country) directly leads to a decrease in the country's population.

questions.question: A measure for preventing the external value of the naira from falling is for the government to

options.A: increase its spending with foreign reserve
options.D: buy its currency with foreign reserve

questions.explanation: To prevent currency depreciation, the government can buy its own currency using foreign reserves, increasing demand for the naira.

questions.question: A fiscal policy instrument that can influence the demand pattern in an economy is
questions.explanation: Tariffs can influence demand patterns by making imported goods more expensive relative to domestic goods.

questions.question: One of the main achievements of the Economic Commission for Africa is

options.C: guaranteeing a steady flow of foreign investment into Africa
options.D: providing the machinery for collaboration on monetary issues

questions.explanation: The Economic Commission for Africa has been instrumental in encouraging transport and communication development across African countries.

questions.question: The rate of interest charge on loans depends largely on

options.C: the risk associated with the loan

questions.explanation: Interest rates on loans are primarily determined by the risk associated with the loan - higher risk leads to higher interest rates.

questions.question: A valid explanation for real wage growth is

options.A: an increase in the rate of productivity
options.B: the rising cost of capital accumulation
options.C: a contraction of employment in service industries
options.D: an increase in the quantity of labour

questions.explanation: Real wage growth is primarily driven by increases in labor productivity, which allows workers to produce more value per hour.

questions.question: If Mr. X lost his clerical job at a store and searched for a similar job for ten months before finding one this implies that Mr. X was
questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment occurs when people are temporarily between jobs while searching for new employment that matches their skills.
